definition: The Second Floor Kitchen and Third Floor Kitchen, respectively. Both are stocked with communal cookware.
Wiess’ courtyard/quad. People commonly hang out, play Frisbee or football, and study here, especially on nice days.
The two giant, covered, swinging picnic tables of glory, located in the Acabowl.
The grills located in the Acabowl.
The terrace connecting the second floor and the Upper Commons.

Affiliate Fellows for new Wiessmen. They are different from Fellows and Co-Fellows, and serve a very important role—not just for your group, but for all the new students. They include your Athlete Affiliate, Diversity Facilitators, Gophers, International Student Liaison, Photographers, and Videographer.
Formal dinner held in the Commons once a semester to honor our Associates.
The terrace behind the Upper Commons that we share with Hanszen.
An affectionate name for the Wiess powderpuff football team.
The governing body of Wiess, made up entirely of Wiessmen. It meets every other Wednesday at 9 pm in the Upper Commons. There’s always free food.
Party to celebrate the new Cabinet each year during the spring semester.
The place to be. You will eat here, study here, act here, play here, party here, hang out here, and well, live here.
A day filled with college bonding, good food, and an evening of entertainment. Each college has their own each semester, usually with a different theme.
To pull up an extra chair at the corner of a table. Frequently occurs during meals.
A corner of the commons featuring extremely comfortable couches, a large goldenrod rug, a small table, and several napping OC students.

Advisors for new Wiessmen. They are some of the greatest people you will ever meet and care about you so much. Co-Fellows are Fellows from other colleges. These other colleges may confuse you by calling them “Advisors,” but we don’t call them that.
A great place to hang out and watch sunsets.
First Tabletop production of the year, which includes, you guessed it, one-acts featuring new students.
Required service hours. Necessary to enter the housing jack at the end of your first year. There are plenty of opportunities throughout the year to get them!
The official Wiess color. It will soon dominate your wardrobe. Remember, it’s not yellow!
The ones who have been planning O-Week since January: Serena, Aditi, and Chichi. Say hello if you see them around!
The process used to assign rooms for the next year.
Called Academic Fellows at other colleges, Wiess Mentors are here to help you in your classes through review/tutoring sessions.
Wiess’ very own movie theater on the fourth floor.
Night of Decadence; Rice’s biggest party. Held at Wiess on the last Saturday of October, it features interesting decorations and creative costumes.
Off-Campus Lounge; a room on the first floor for Off-Campus students.
The loud speakers that can be heard throughout the Acabowl on Friday afternoons or special occasions.
The weekend retreat to Galveston during the fall semester to bond with other Wiessmen.
Our cheer. It is one of our oldest traditions, and an embodiment of the spirit Wiess has always been known for.
An abbreviation of Team Family (or anything else that starts with F) Wiess.
Private Dining Room; a room attached to the Commons.
Team Fun Friday Wiess. Held every other week, this event features food and fun for everyone in the Acabowl. What other colleges call Friday in the Quad.
The week preceding Beer Bike, filled with college activities, alumni, and jacks.
A unique Wiess celebration of life. If you have any questions, just ask a friendly Wiessman.
The spreading of Halloween cheer, led by the elected College Idiots. Features Halloween songs and visits to the other colleges.
Second floor of the Commons featuring a pool table, ping pong table, foosball table, TV, and lots of couches.
Where you get your food before you go sit down in the Commons. We share South Servery with Hanszen.
Wiess mascot; embodied by the giant wooden pig built by the Class of 2012 for Beer Bike.
Nestled in a corner on the fourth floor, this goldenrod room emblazoned with a massive Wiess crest features great views and is a fun place to hang out.
Wiess theatre productions, held in the Commons.
Flavio and Fabiana’s home. Where everybody knows your name, and the door is always open.
The inclusive, gender-neutral term for all members of Wiess—including you.
A day to celebrate Wiess held in the Acabowl during the spring semester.
The three slabs of granite located in the Engineering Quad, worth three million dollars and modeled after their namesake angles.
Humanities or Social Sciences major. A very archaic term.
A modernistic glass building located behind Fondren. Home to Little Kitchen (a non-student operated bakery and café) and a great place to relax and sit outside.
The central academic quadrangle surrounding Willy’s Statue.
Architecture student.
Alternative Spring Break; a service trip over spring break based on a social issue.
Faculty, staff, or community member associated with a college. Good people to get to know.
Gym in Tudor Fieldhouse where the Rice basketball teams play.

An event where participants undress, smear shaving cream on their bodies, and run around campus, leaving a trail of body prints. A proud Baker tradition for over thirty years; all undergrads are invited to participate.
The James A. Baker III Institute for Public Policy. Holds many interesting talks and events that are typically open to undergraduates. Not to be confused with Baker College.

A competitive intercollege race held in the spring, where ten bikers and ten chuggers from each college compete for both personal and college pride. Often compared to Christmas, it also includes a water balloon fight and much rejoicing.
The “real world” outside of Rice.
The classes frequently taken by Natural Sciences and Engineering majors: Physics, Chemistry, and Calculus.
BioScience Research Collaborative, where Rice meets the Texas Medical Center for research. Also where Bioengineers spend most of their time for class starting junior year.
1. The bell tower in the Engineering Quad. 2. Rice’s yearbook. 3. The undergraduate orchestra for non-music majors.
An affectionate name for Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering majors.
Student-run coffeeshop providing the best legal way to artificially increase your study skills on short notice. Located in the RMC.
The faculty dining club near Sewall Hall with really good food.
Critical Thinking in Sexuality. A required course for new students to provide information about consent, relationships, and bystander training.

Refers to distribution credits, Rice’s way of making sure you get a balanced education. You need at least 9 credit hours in each category to graduate. D1 = Humanities, D2 = Social Sciences, and D3 = Science and Engineering.
The fall formal hosted by Rice Program Council. A major part of homecoming weekend and lots of fun!

Also known as Club Fondy, Fondren is Rice’s library—it has seminar rooms, study rooms, and classrooms that you can reserve. It is a great place for productivity or a quick nap between classes, and it’s open 24 hours a day during the week.
An architectural quirk of Anderson Hall. Running your hand down the ridges of the wall produces a frog-like noise. Try it out for yourself.
First-Year Writing-Intensive Seminar. Writing course students are required to take in their first year. Rhymes with “swiss.”
Graduate Student Association.
Housing and Dining. The Administrative office in charge of all food service and residential buildings on campus.
Extensive botanical growth that surrounds campus and the Academic Quad.
Someone who both bikes and chugs at Beer Bike.
The area in the Medical Center with many restaurants that Rice students frequent.
A prank pulled on another college.
Rice’s Graduate School of Business, not to be confused with Jones College.
Rice’s student-run radio station, which now streams online. Plays everything from jazz to reggae to bands you probably didn’t even know existed.
Lifetime Physical Activity Program. A required “gym” class that all students must take to graduate. Capoeira, swing dance, fencing, and yoga are among the many different options.
The ceremony held during O-Week to officially welcome you to Rice.
A student-run late night food stop for hungry students which is located in the RMC.
The building near West Lot and RUPD where film and photography classes are held. Also houses a gallery space and theatre with Houston’s only silver screen.

Intramural. Informal, low-stress sports played among students. Not to be confused with college sports, which are played between teams representing each of the colleges with points going towards the President’s Cup.
The one-way road that loops around the center of campus.
The university computer center. If you have problems with your computer, the IT (Information Technology) people here are glad to help out. Also a great place to print large posters.
Marching Owl Band. They don’t actually march. They do, however, always put on an entertaining show during halftime—filled with amusing skits, jibes at opposing teams, and zany antics.
Music student.
Off-campus. Typically your second year at Wiess.
The three-mile long path that encircles [the entry breaks off here in the book]
Peer Academic Advisors. Students who are trained by the Office of Academic Advising to help you choose classes and navigate Rice academics.

Peer Career Advisors. Students who are trained by the Center for Career Development. They can help you revise your resume or cover letter, as well as figure out resources to find internships and jobs.
An independent literary magazine published entirely by students.
Barbara and David Gibbs Recreation and Wellness Center. Fully equipped for all of your workout needs. Also where the Wellbeing and Counseling Center is located.
Convenience store located in the RMC.
A party thrown by a group of people, rather than the whole college. The rules and regulations vary with each college but they are outlined in the Alcohol Policy.
Women’s college flag football. One of the most intense (and fun) college sports, as well as a great spectator sport. Played in the fall semester.
Courses or credits needed prior to signing up for a course.
Willy’s Pub, located in the basement of the RMC. A great place to grab some pizza and hang out with people across campus. Heavily populated on Thursday nights.
Rice University Emergency Medical Services. Rice students that are trained as Emergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) who respond to emergencies on campus.
Rice Health Advisor. Students who are passionate about being healthy and keeping their fellow students healthy too!
Rice Memorial Center; where you can find the Bookstore, Coffeehouse, Pub, and important offices like Academic Advising.
Spring formal hosted by Rice Program Council.
Rice Program Council. The organization in charge of university-wide events such as Beer Bike, Screw-Yer-Roommate, Esperanza, and study breaks during finals.
Rice Student Volunteer Program. The organization that runs many community service opportunities beyond the hedges.
Rice University Police Department. Save their number for emergencies: 713-348-6000.
A party thrown by a residential college (most throw one a semester). All of them are themed and open to all undergrads.
A harsh penalty banning a student from campus except for attending classes and exams. Basically, don’t get rusticated.
Mid-semester grades given to new students in the fall to indicate how they are doing in their classes. They come out around Halloween.
The card that gets you on the lightrail. Works for the Metro Bus system too.
Student Association. The campus-wide body representing students. Deals with campus-wide issues and administrative business.
The big archway in Lovett Hall. Rumor says that if you walk through it between matriculation and graduation, you won’t graduate.
Southern slang short for “you all.” Soon enough, y’all will be saying this too. (It’s efficient!)
The Rice mascot.
Also known as Screw. A Rice tradition held in the fall in which roommates set up blind dates for each other.
The pyramidal installation located next to the Shepherd School of Music. A reat place to watch the sunrise and sunset.
Student Maintenance Representative. The liaison between H&D and the students. They can help you change the height of your bed or your lightbulbs.
“Digital Money” on your ID card that can be used at various on-campus venues such as: The Hoot, Coffeehouse, Pub, Sammy’s, Brochstein, and the serveries. Usually referred to simply as Tetra.
Rice’s weekly student newspaper.
The graduate student bar located below Keck Hall which serves cheap beer and lunch on the weekdays.
The shopping center west of campus. Has a lot of great restaurants and shops, all within walking distance!
A 24-hour restaurant where you can get a burger or legendary Honey Butter Chicken Biscuit.
Your home and family.
(table) Baker—Bakerite; Will Rice—Will Ricer; Hanszen—Hanszenite; Jones—Jonesian; Brown—Brownie; Lovett—Lovetteer; Sid Richardson—Sidizen; Martel—Martelian; McMurtry—Murt; Duncan—Duncaroo.
